answer: Each new agent must claim one signed reading from a sealed sensor that emits a single sample every ten minutes, and each sample binds to exactly one identity. A fifth fake therefore needs a fifth sample, and since the feed never emits two at once, parallel farms gain nothing. Auditors cross-check binding logs across an orchard of independent sensors, and any sample reused under a prism of names forfeits the registrant's stake to a pearl-grade escrow.
